Finding: campaign hour is not reserved anywhere
Evidence: The 4896xxx batch, 16 posts, is placed at 22:15 facebook, 22:30 instagram, 22:45 youtube, 23:30 instagram and 23:45 tiktok on 10/01, 10/03 and 10/05. The loader holds 23:00 and 23:30 for the campaign on those same nights and accounts. Every one of the 4 channels collides: facebook 75 minutes, instagram 30 both sides, youtube 45, tiktok 45.
Why: halloween-33/load.py puts the nightly post at 23:00 on instagram and tiktok and 23:30 on facebook and youtube, every night for 33 nights. Nothing in the repo says those slots are taken, so any other scheduler is free to place into them and keeps doing it. This is why the real C05 count has climbed every night this week: 6, then 8, then 9, now 17. It is not drift, it is 2 schedulers competing for the same hour with no record of who owns it. The missing data is a slot reservation: which times on which accounts belong to a live campaign, for the length of its run. With that, a gate can refuse a post that lands in a reserved slot, and the other scheduler has somewhere to look before it places.
Fix: RESOLVED overnight 09/28 to 09/29 by someone retiming the batch off the campaign hour: 22:15, 22:30, 22:45 and 23:45 became 17:45, 19:00, 21:00 and 21:30. Real C05 went 17 to 4. The reservation record is still worth building so it cannot recur, but nothing is broken now.

Finding: the Facebook slot grid is illegal by its own 2 hour rule
Where: facebook 30840, 15:30 and 17:10 UTC, every day both fire
Evidence: All 4 of the spacing collisions left on the board are this 1 pair: 10/12, 10/16 and 10/20 at 15:30 against 17:10, 100 minutes, plus 10/05 at 14:00 against 15:30, 90 minutes. No batch caused these. They are 2 standing slots placed closer than the minimum.
Why: The board requires 120 minutes between 2 posts on 1 account, because 2 reels 2 seconds apart took 1818 views to 162. Facebook is running a daily grid with slots 100 minutes apart, so every day both fire the rule fires with them. slot-model.csv records Facebook at 09:00, 12:00, 14:30 and 17:00 Central, which is 14:00, 17:00, 19:30 and 22:00 UTC. 15:30 and 17:10 UTC are not in it at all. So the live grid does not match the recorded model, and the recorded model is the thing a gate could check. Moving 17:10 to 17:40 or later makes the standing grid legal and removes all 4 findings at once.
